I farm only 5 mu, so I count money carefully, but I still will not save too much on fertilizer because if cotton gets weak early, I cannot make that yield back later. I usually start from what I did before and then look at water and prices. In our place in Quzhou, spring cotton needs a strong base fertilizer, then I topdress again when squares and bolls come. I have well water, so I will use that advantage and not let the field stay dry at the key stages. I will plant improved seed this year, because I have seen the newer kinds stand better and yield more evenly than old saved seed. For tillage, I will plough first, because cotton likes loose soil and good rooting, and old hands around me still do that on serious cotton land. On fertilizer, I will not go light: I will put enough phosphorus under the crop at the start, then keep nitrogen and potassium for later growth and boll filling. On pests, cotton here cannot be left alone, so I will spray when needed, mainly for aphids, mites, and bollworms, and I expect about 5 sprays in a normal year. If the weather is normal and I manage water on time, I will aim for about 360 kg seed cotton per mu.
